text:
maya: quick question — we're seeing a couple of customer bugs from the node sdk where streaming responses throw a generic Error and there's no request id in logs. anyone else run into this?

sam: yep saw one yesterday. looks like when the stream connection fails mid-llm-call we surface a plain `Error: stream closed` from the ws layer, lost the x-request-id from the header.

binji: is this the new retry work or the old backoff middleware?

maya: node client 0.12.1, streaming + auth via bearer token. not retries — the client doesn't get to retry because the connection aborted. we should still map the API error to a shaped exception and attach the rid.

elin: quick take: we should ensure the low-level connection layer copies the `x-request-id` returned by the server into the error object before bubbling up. In go we have a typed `APIError` that contains Rid and Code, so it's easier. in node we usually only have `Error` unless we wrap it.

sam: agree. proposal: on any non-200/aborted stream, create a `RedwoodApiError` with: `message`, `code`, `rid`, `status`, and `original` (for stack). For streaming aborts, populate `code: \"stream_aborted\"`.

maya: can we also standardize the header name? Some infra services use `x-request-id`, others `x-rid`. maybe the SDK should check both and normalize to `request_id` on the error object.

binji: +1. Also we need a debug flag that includes the raw transport headers in logs. helps customers file support tickets without us repro-ing.

elin: in go client we already set `error.RequestID` and log it via zap. For py and node, we should add small helpers. For python: `raise RedwoodApiError(msg, code=code, rid=rid) from exc` so tracebacks chain.

sam: code snippet for node wrapper i suggested:

```
// pseudo
function makeError(resp, headers, orig) {
  const rid = headers['x-request-id'] || headers['x-rid'] || null;
  const err = new Error(resp.message || 'request failed');
  err.code = resp.code || 'unknown_error';
  err.rid = rid;
  err.status = resp.status || 0;
  err.original = orig;
  return err;
}
```

maya: this is perfect. can we also wire the retry middleware to look for `err.code === 'stream_aborted'` and do a single reconnect attempt for streaming calls? some customers expect resume.

elin: streaming resume is tricky unless we provide a resume token. fallback behavior should be: if `stream_aborted` and `idempotent: true` then retry once. SDKs should mark which routes are idempotent in the route meta.

binji: QA note — when we retry, include the original rid in `x-forwarded-rid` header so we can connect logs across attempts.

maya: logging guidance for support: include `request_id`, `model`, `route`, `attempt`, and trimmed `prompt` (not full user PII). maybe expose `REDWOOD_CLIENT_DEBUG=1` to dump these automatically.

sam: can we add an opt-in where the SDK attaches `client-request-id` (generated UUID) to every call so users can map client logs to server rid? server already echoes it.

elin: yes we already echo `client-request-id` in hosted api — but not consistently in Dedicated. infra ticket opened last week to propagate.

ci-bot: deployment notice: go-client v0.8.3 will include `APIError` shape and `request_id` plumbing — rolling canary today 18:00 PT.

maya: excellent. action items:
- sam: implement node `RedwoodApiError` wrapper + header normalization (priority).
- elin: add python chaining example to sdk docs and sample snippet for resume/retry heuristics.
- benji: coordinate infra to ensure `x-request-id` vs `x-rid` canonicalization across gateways.

benji: I'll sync infra; ETA EOD.
sam: i'll put a tiny PR up for node by lunchtime my time. ping me on review pls.

elin: i'll open a docs PR and include a small README section: \"How to interpret errors and find request ids\" with examples for go/py/node.

maya: thanks everyone. small follow-up: add unit tests that assert `err.rid` is present for failed stream and that `client-request-id` gets echoed.

benji: noted — will add infra test and a smoke test in the e2e harness.

maya: :thumbsup:

sam: one more edge case — auth handshake fails (401) during stream handshake. please map 401 to `AuthError` class that includes `rid` and `token_expired` bool when `www-authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\"` appears.

elin: good catch. will add header parsing for `www-authenticate` into auth middleware.

maya: cool. i'll file a small trello ticket with the checklist. thanks!
